## AI-Generated Fix (javascript)

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
const port = 8882;

// Middleware to sanitize input
const sanitizeInput = (req, res, next) => {
  for (let key in req.query) {
    req.query[key] = req.query[key].replace(/<[^>]*>?/gm, '');
  }
  for (let key in req.body) {
    req.body[key] = req.body[key].replace(/<[^>]*>?/gm, '');
  }
  next();
};

app.use(express.json());
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));
app.use(sanitizeInput);

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.send('Hello, sanitized world!');
});

app.listen(port, () => {
  console.log(`Server running at http://34.16.47.248:${port}/`);
});
```

---

## Explanation

The vulnerability was due to unsanitized user input being processed and potentially rendered on the web application, which could lead to XSS attacks. The fix involves adding a middleware function that sanitizes all incoming query and body parameters by removing any HTML tags, thus preventing malicious scripts from being executed.
